rewrite.screen.help-records.must.1: Answer within {days} days whether it holds records it can release, why or why not, and when they will be ready ({cite}).
rewrite.screen.help-records.must.2: Take longer only by written notice, saying why and when, for reasons the law lists ({reasons}); never more than {extra} extra days ({cite}).
rewrite.screen.help-records.must.3: Help you focus the request: identify the records that fit it, say where they are kept, and suggest ways past practical obstacles ({cite}).
rewrite.screen.help-records.must.4: Release the rest of a record that is partly exempt ({cite}), and refuse only in writing, naming who decided ({cite2}).
rewrite.screen.help-records.must.5: Give electronic records electronically, in a format it keeps them in, when you ask ({cite}).
rewrite.screen.help-records.must.6: Charge only the direct cost of copying ({cite}); for electronic records, of producing the copy, unless it must compile, extract or program data ({cite2}). You may photograph records you inspect, with your own equipment, at no charge ({cite3}).
rewrite.screen.help-records.must.7: Never ask why you want them: access can't be limited because of the purpose of a request ({cite}).
rewrite.screen.help-records.portal.2: Each request's page shows its full text to anyone, with its dates, the department and the city's contact. Write the request so you are content for anyone to read it.
rewrite.screen.help-records.portal.3: Contact details are optional. Without them you get no updates, and you can collect the records only if the department posts them publicly or you contact it yourself.

rewrite.screen.join.handle.help: The record shows your handle on your work. Choose it with care: it can't be changed after you join, and no one else can ever take it. It needn't be your legal name. Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, 2 to 41 of them, starting with a letter or digit. Choosing a handle: a name people know lends your work credibility and lets reporters reach you, but puts it on public cases; a pen name shields you from pressure, while the administrators still know who you are.
rewrite.screen.join.codes.after: When you join, you get ten recovery codes, shown once: save them, they are how you get back in if you forget your password. Then you are signed in and your team's home opens, with a short guided start you can take or leave.

rewrite.screen.recovery.held: You hold recovery codes: {remaining} of {total} unused, issued {date}.
rewrite.screen.recovery.shown: Save these now: they are shown only this once. Keep them somewhere only you can reach, apart from your password. Civicsmith keeps only a fingerprint of each, so it can never show them again.
rewrite.screen.reset.keeps: Your handle and everything you did stay as they are, and every other sign-in of yours ends. {name} can't see the password you choose. Your recovery codes still work; if you have lost them too, get ten new ones in Settings › Recovery codes once you are in.
rewrite.screen.reset.dead.what: It was used already, it expired, or an administrator withdrew it. Ask an administrator for a new one, in person or however your team talks. Nothing was changed.
rewrite.screen.review-copy.heading: Share Edition {edition} for review
rewrite.screen.review-outside.heading: A review copy from {group}
rewrite.screen.request.describe: Describe the records, not why you want them. The law doesn't let the office limit access because of why you ask ({cite}), and the city's portal shows this text to anyone.
rewrite.screen.request.howsend.1: Open the city's public records portal ({portal}) and choose “{button}”.
rewrite.screen.request.howsend.2: Paste the approved text as the request description, and choose the department: {department}.
rewrite.screen.request.howsend.3: Contact details are optional. Without them the request still goes in, but the city can't send you updates or ask you to clarify, and you can't sign in to collect the records. Give the address your team uses for its requests; staff see what you give.
rewrite.screen.standard.notyet: Not a standard until a member adopts it.
rewrite.screen.ties.says.name.choice: Naming me by my handle: “{handle}, who worked on this case, is {tie}.”
rewrite.screen.ties.says.group.choice: Without naming me: “A member of the team who worked on this case is {tie}.”
rewrite.screen.timeline.order.evidence: More evidence could order them: a passage that gives either one its day (a ledger entry, a meeting's agenda, a letter's date), or a source that says which came first. Until a source orders them, both are kept as they are, never guessed into order; when one does, the timeline names it, and a source that disagrees is shown beside it, in tension.
rewrite.shell.unavailable.nothing.says: This address doesn't lead to anything in your team's Civicsmith. It may have been typed wrong, or the link is old.
rewrite.shell.unavailable.notyours.says: It exists, or it may not: either way it isn't something you can see. A hidden project shows only to its own members; ask its owner if you think you should be in it.
rewrite.shell.unavailable.unreachable.title: Your team's Civicsmith can't be reached
rewrite.shell.unavailable.unreachable.says: Your device is offline, or your team's Civicsmith isn't answering. Nothing you did is lost: what you saved is kept there, and what you were typing is still on this page.
rewrite.screen.wizards.copy.note: A copy becomes your team's own wizard: a draft until approved, like any wizard your team writes. The original stays as it is and is still offered; a required wizard stays required. The copy shows what it is based on, and when Civicsmith's original changes, your wizard editors are told and can bring the change across.
rewrite.screen.setup.lede: Welcome. Civicsmith is installed and waiting for you. First, claim it, so that only you can run it; it takes about two minutes. Then tell it a little about your team. Only the claim is needed today: every other part starts with a safe choice, and you can change any of it later in Settings.
rewrite.screen.setup.otp.help: Already filled in if you came straight from the installer.
rewrite.screen.setup.handle.help: The name you sign in with, shown on your work and on every case you sign. Choose it with care: it can't be changed later.
rewrite.screen.setup.own.help: At least 12 characters. From now on you sign in with your handle and this password.
rewrite.screen.setup.name.help: Shown at the top of every page, on invitations and on everything your team publishes. You can change it any time.
rewrite.screen.setup.name.now: Saved. Your team is now called {name}.
rewrite.screen.setup.domain.help: Civicsmith gives you one small file to put on your website. Once it's there, anyone reading what your team publishes can check that it really comes from you. Whoever looks after your website can do this in a few minutes.
rewrite.screen.setup.places.help: Not listed? Choose “Somewhere else”. Everything still works; you enter deadlines and offices yourself.
rewrite.screen.setup.places.chosen: You chose {place} when you installed. Change it if you need to.
rewrite.screen.setup.place.wanted.help: When an update brings its rules, Civicsmith tells you, and you can switch to it here. What you type stays in your team's Civicsmith and is never sent anywhere.
rewrite.screen.setup.offices.what: Civicsmith can fill in the public offices of {place}, and who holds each one today, from the place's own records. Check the list, then confirm it. You can add others at any time.
rewrite.screen.setup.offices.none: Civicsmith doesn't know the offices of {place} yet, so this list starts empty. Add the offices your team deals with, now or whenever they come up. When an update brings their rules, you'll be told, and the offices you added stay.
rewrite.screen.setup.office.note: Anything your team should know about it (optional)
rewrite.screen.setup.assistant.what: Civicsmith can include an AI assistant, built on Anthropic's Claude. Members ask it, in everyday words, to find, read and check things in your team's material. It works only from what your team holds, gives legal information but never legal advice, and never decides, signs or sends anything. Everything in Civicsmith also works without it.
rewrite.screen.setup.keepaway: No, keep our material away from AI
rewrite.screen.setup.keepaway.help: Required. Every member will see it.
rewrite.screen.setup.assistant.own: A member who wants the assistant connects their own Claude subscription or API key. It serves only them, at their own cost, and costs your team nothing.
rewrite.screen.setup.assistant.paid: One Anthropic API key, paid for by your team, serves every member who has no account of their own. A member's own account still comes first.
rewrite.screen.setup.key.help: Made in Anthropic's Console, under an account your team pays for. Civicsmith locks it away and never shows it again.
rewrite.screen.setup.limit: The most each member may use per day
rewrite.screen.setup.limit.help: Applies only to your team's key, never to a member's own account. More limits are in Settings › Members.
rewrite.screen.setup.people.what: Facts about a person that come from public documents are as visible as those documents are. Your team's own notes about a person stay inside the project where they were written.
rewrite.screen.setup.court.what: Civicsmith keeps your team's unpublished work private, from the public and from the people you look into. But a court order your team can't defeat can still require anything not public to be shown, such as members' notes, sources and hidden projects. Much work never draws such an order, and journalists, lawyers and auditors may have protections others lack.
rewrite.screen.setup.court.legend: Should members be told about this?
rewrite.screen.setup.court.tell: Yes, when they join, and the first time they save something not public
rewrite.screen.setup.court.dont: No, just keep the explanation one tap away
rewrite.screen.setup.admins.what: Right now you're the only administrator. If you're away or lose access, no one else can run your team's Civicsmith. Invite someone you trust as a second administrator, now or later.
rewrite.screen.setup.security.scanner: Civicsmith's own file scanner checks every file your team brings in, and risky ones open in a safe view. You don't need to do anything.
rewrite.screen.setup.security.what: If your organization already uses its own file scanner, a tool that makes safe copies of files, or a log service, you can connect it here or later in Settings › Security.
rewrite.screen.setup.finished.what: Anything you left is waiting in Settings. Next, invite your first members.
rewrite.act.queuemute.does: Stops this kind of item, or a project's items, reaching your queue, or lets muted ones reach it again. What you muted is listed under Muted at the foot of your queue.
rewrite.act.promote.does: Turns what you are looking at into something the team will work on: a hint, chain or suggestion into a question, or a problem into a project. Where it came from is kept with it.
rewrite.project.visibility.start.later: Choose one: neither is chosen for you. You can change it later, with a reason.
rewrite.screen.updates.admins: Only your team's administrators install updates. Yours: {admins}. If something needs updating, ask one of them.
rewrite.screen.security.admins: Security is set by your team's administrators. Yours: {admins}. Ask one of them about anything here.
rewrite.question.empty.heading: Next: bring in a source
rewrite.question.empty.note: A question is answered from documents: your government's own records, a report, what a member saw. Start with one; you can add more at any time.
rewrite.question.empty.capture.line: Its web address, a file, or what you saw yourself. Civicsmith keeps the copy for you to confirm, then you mark the part that answers.
rewrite.question.empty.find.line: Search the team's documents, open one, and mark the part that answers.
rewrite.question.empty.ask.line: It reads what the team holds and suggests the parts that answer, and an answer. Nothing counts until a member accepts it.
rewrite.stake.none: No stake of its own beyond the team's
rewrite.screen.review-copy.until.nozone: Your team's time zone isn't set, and a review link's end date is counted in it. Set it under Settings, Your team, then share.
